source: Kim, Kang, Kim, Yang, Ren, Hwang (2026) Memory Transfer Learning: How Memories are Transferred Across Domains in Coding Agents
finding: Memories made on other coding benchmarks (not the target one) raised a current small model's average score. Gains came from meta-knowledge (validation routines, workflow discipline), not from task code.
numbers: GPT-5-mini, six benchmarks (LiveCodeBench v6, Aider-Polyglot, SWE-Bench Verified, TerminalBench2, ReplicationBench, MLGym), Pass@3, 3 runs, 3 memories retrieved per query. Average: zero-shot 0.523; Trajectory 0.534; Workflow 0.538; Summary 0.546; Insight 0.560 (+3.7 points). Insight gains up to +8.3 points (MLGym) and +7.8 (ReplicationBench); 0.0 on Aider-Polyglot. Other models: DeepSeek V3.2 +2.6 average, Qwen3-Coder-480B +1.8.
limits: Pass@3 on small benchmarks (MLGym about 12 tasks). No token-matched control; memory adds context. PDF table text is garbled; averages cross-checked against the stated +3.7. Cross-domain here means a different benchmark in the same tool and language family.
agent_relevance: Best direct answer to gap 1: a lesson store built on OTHER task sets lifts a current model by a few points, so the effect is cross-class, not near-duplicate retrieval. Expect +2 to +4 points, not more. Supports O7 lesson reuse across classes if lessons are written as insights.

source: Kim et al. (2026) Memory Transfer Learning, comparison with in-domain memory systems (Table 2) and retrieval ablation (Table 7)
finding: A small cross-domain pool (431 memories) beat in-domain ReasoningBank (97) and a large general AgentKB pool (5,899). Model-judged reranking and rewriting did worse than plain embedding similarity.
numbers: GPT-5-mini, Pass@3 on LCB / SWE-Bench / ReplicationBench. Zero-shot 0.584 average; ReasoningBank 0.601; AgentKB 0.613; MTL 0.630. Retrieval ablation: no memory 0.584; LLM reranking of 20 candidates 0.598; LLM task-adaptive rewriting 0.608; embedding similarity 0.630.
limits: Same small benchmark set. Reranking and rewriting are model-judged, not code-checked.
agent_relevance: Gap 2 partial: letting the model judge which lessons match did not beat cheap embedding retrieval (-3.2 and -2.2 points). Model-judged matching is not a free precision gain. A typed, code-checked mapping is still untested.

source: Kim et al. (2026) Memory Transfer Learning, abstraction analysis (Table 4, Finding 3) and negative-transfer analysis (Section 4.4.1, Finding 4)
finding: More abstract memories transferred better. Concrete traces could produce negative transfer. The authors examined cases where zero-shot succeeded and memory failed, and named three causes.
numbers: Task-agnostic insights (bottom 30% by task similarity) 0.534 average vs task-specific insights (top 30%) 0.523, +1.1 points (LCB 0.893 vs 0.887; SWE 0.627 vs 0.617; ReplicationBench 0.082 vs 0.067). Format order by average: Insight 0.560 > Summary 0.546 > Workflow 0.538 > Trajectory 0.534. Causes of harm: domain-mismatched anchoring (superficially similar, structurally irrelevant), false validation confidence, misapplied best-practice transfer. Two cited failures: an R-language file routine applied in C++; a validation insight read as licence for a shortcut.
quote: Structurally irrelevant but superficially similar memories act as misleading anchors
limits: Differences of 1 to 3 points on small n; no confidence intervals. Abstraction was measured by embedding spread, not by token count.
agent_relevance: Gaps 4, 6 and 10 partial. Abstract lines beat concrete traces by small margins; harm from surface-similar memories is real and was observed on tasks the plain model solved. Add a check that the lesson's stated precondition holds before applying it.

source: Hu, Long, Wang (2026) When Continual Learning Moves to Memory: A Study of Experience Reuse in LLM Agents
finding: Raw trajectories from task A hurt on a related task B. LLM-abstracted insights helped. The harm fell on the cases the plain agent could not solve.
numbers: ALFWorld A (pick_and_place, baseline 95%) to B (pick_clean_place, baseline 54%): Raw memory forward transfer -9.5 points (80.5 to 71.0), change on baseline-fail subset -26.1; Insight +6.5 (65.5 to 72.0), baseline-fail subset +3.3. BabyAI A (action_obj_door, 70%) to B (find_obj, 49%): Raw -7.5 (53.5 to 46.0), baseline-fail subset -12.7; Insight +9.0 (46.0 to 55.0), baseline-fail subset +9.8. Baseline-success subset change for Raw: +4.6 ALFWorld, -2.0 BabyAI.
quote: Raw trajectories tend to hinder adaptation to new tasks, while abstract insights are safer to reuse
limits: Two task pairs only. Backbone model not identified in the parts I read. Table columns read as printed (T, X to T, FWT, RR, NL); the T column appears to be a within-task memory score.
agent_relevance: Gaps 6 and 10 partial. Cost of wrong reuse is large for concrete traces on hard items (up to -26 points) and small on already-solved items (at most -2). Einstellung-style breakage of solved problems looks minor here; the damage is failing to rescue hard ones. Prefer insight-level lessons for cross-class reuse.

source: Qiu et al. (2026) LifeMem: Enabling Lifelong Experience Reuse for LLM Agents, zero-shot transfer (Table 4) and backbone effect
finding: On unseen task formulations and unseen environments, concrete-trajectory memory baselines sometimes fell below the no-memory agent. Abstracted, environment-invariant skills did not. Gains were larger for the weaker backbone.
numbers: FEVER (new task, same environment), GPT-4o-mini: ReAct 0.40, Synapse 0.38, ExpeL 0.41, AutoSkill 0.49, LifeMem 0.49 (+22.5%). tau-bench airline (new environment, similar task), GPT-4o-mini: ReAct 0.32, Synapse 0.26, ExpeL 0.26, AutoSkill 0.34, LifeMem 0.38 (+18.8%). DeepSeek-v3.2-exp airline: ReAct 0.38, Synapse 0.40, ExpeL 0.42, LifeMem 0.44; FEVER: ReAct 0.39, ExpeL 0.32, AutoSkill 0.36, LifeMem 0.46. Overall across five scenarios: GPT-4o-mini 28.84 to 44.13; DeepSeek-v3.2-exp 41.14 to 48.02.
limits: Small test sets (scores move in steps of 0.01 to 0.05); backbones are mid-tier, not 2026 frontier; the method is the authors' own.
agent_relevance: Gaps 1 and 6: negative transfer from raw experience is measurable (-0.06 on airline for two baselines, -0.07 for ExpeL on DeepSeek FEVER). Gain shrinks with a stronger backbone (+15.3 vs +6.9 points), so expect a modest lesson-reuse lift for a frontier model.

source: Wu et al. (2026) MemHarness: Memory Is Reconstructed, Not Replayed (Table 3, ALFWorld OOD)
finding: With a trained policy that was already strong, injecting unadapted memories lowered success under layout shift. Reconstructing the memory against the current state recovered and exceeded the no-memory level.
numbers: ALFWorld OOD average success: MemHarness 85.9; no memory 83.0; memory without reconstruction 82.4; RL plus raw memory 76.3. Mechanism check: a random mismatched state raises rejection of memories from 8.7 to 13.3% (ALFWorld) and 56.0 to 63.3% (WebShop).
limits: Needs GRPO training of the policy; not a prompt-only result. The 0.6 point gap is likely within noise.
agent_relevance: Gap 10: nearest sign of 'a stored lesson harms a model that would have done fine' (-0.6 unadapted, -6.7 raw memory plus RL). The fix, critique the memory against the current state before use, is a prompt-level step O7 can copy.

source: Xiong et al. (2025) How Memory Management Impacts LLM Agents: An Empirical Study of Experience-Following Behavior
finding: Agents copy the output of the most similar stored case. High input similarity gives high output similarity, so wrong stored cases propagate (error propagation) and correct-looking but misaligned cases mislead (misaligned replay).
numbers: Selective addition plus history-based deletion beat naive growth (authors report about 10% average gain; I did not re-derive it). Strict-evaluator deletion in AgentDriver even beat an error-free memory baseline.
limits: Read text and figure captions; per-benchmark tables not transcribed. Tasks are EHRAgent, AgentDriver, RegAgent, not reasoning problems.
agent_relevance: Gap 6: surface-similarity retrieval plus copying is the mechanism of false-match harm. A lesson store needs deletion by measured utility and a precondition check before reuse.

source: Wang, Mao, Fried, Neubig (2024) Agent Workflow Memory (AWM), Mind2Web cross-task, cross-website and cross-domain splits (Table 4) and WebArena cross-template (Table 2)
finding: Re-bucketed by distance, AWM gains persist across all three distances in step-level success, but full-task success stays near the floor at the far buckets.
numbers: Mind2Web, GPT-4. Step SR: cross-task MindAct 36.2, AWM offline 45.1, AWM online 43.6 (+8.9, +7.4). Cross-website 30.1, 33.7, 33.9 (+3.6, +3.8). Cross-domain 18.6, 32.6, 35.5 (+14.0, +16.9). Full-task SR: cross-task 2.0, 4.8, 4.0; cross-website 2.0, 2.3, 1.6; cross-domain 1.0, 0.7, 1.7. WebArena cross-template subset (one random task per template): total SR AWM 33.2 vs AutoEval 23.2 and BrowserGym 20.5; SteP with human workflows 32.1.
limits: Cross-domain step gain is largest partly because that baseline is lowest; task-level success is 0.7 to 4.8%, too small to rank. Offline workflows came from the training set, online from the test stream. The cross-template table has no matched no-workflow row.
agent_relevance: Gap 7 partial: AWM is not only same-template reuse (cross-template WebArena and Mind2Web cross-domain both show gains), but the gain does not turn into solved tasks at long distance. Report lesson reuse by distance bucket as K23 says.

source: Sourati, Ilievski, Sommerauer, Jiang (2024) ARN: Analogical Reasoning on Narratives (TACL), Table 2 and text
finding: Re-read the headline numbers. The 39.6% is an average across all tested models on far analogies; humans were 94.1%. GPT-4 zero-shot was above chance on (far, far) pairs but low when the distractor was a near disanalogy.
numbers: 1,096 triples. Zero-shot accuracy by partition (near,far / near,near / far,far / far,near / average): GPT-4 94.0 / 92.5 / 57.1 / 29.1 / 68.1; GPT-3.5 88.1 / 81.3 / 50.4 / 21.7 / 60.3; SBERT 84.3 / 71.5 / 12.6 / 1.0 / 42.3; all-model average 76.9 / 73.2 / 45.3 / 33.9 / 57.3; humans 98.6 / 97.2 / 96.8 / 91.4 / 96.0. Models average 75.0% on near analogies vs 97.9% for humans; 39.6% on far analogies vs 94.1%. Random baseline 50%.
quote: models only achieved 39.6% on average (worse than random performance) when solving far analogies
limits: Models are 2023-era (GPT-4.0, GPT-3.5, Llama-2, FlanT5, UnifiedQA, Macaw). No reasoning model tested. Few-shot with CoT raised far-analogy accuracy but hurt near.
agent_relevance: Gap 3: the 2024 numbers are confirmed, and they show surface-similar distractors are the failure, which is the case against a lesson store keyed on surface text. No ARN number for o-series, Claude 4+ or Gemini 2.5+ was found, so gap 3 stays open.

source: Beger et al. (2026) Distinguishing Performance From Competence in Evaluations of Humanlike Abstract Reasoning (ConceptARC; o3, Gemini 2.5 Pro, Claude Sonnet 4)
finding: Reasoning models now match humans on text ConceptARC grid accuracy, but a large share of their correct answers rest on shallow or unintended rules rather than the intended abstraction.
numbers: Pass@1 textual: o3 medium effort 77.1 (68.3 low), o3 medium + Python 75.6; Claude Sonnet 4 60.2 (55.0 with tools); Gemini 2.5 Pro 66.0 (60.4 with tools); humans 73.0. About 27% of o3's correct textual outputs used correct-unintended or incorrect rules vs about 7% for humans. Visual: o3 29.2 (with tools), Claude 6.9, Gemini 5.8; correct-intended rules 40.0%, 14.4%, 23.5%.
limits: ConceptARC tests concept abstraction within grids, not story-level far analogy. About 19% of human rules were unclassifiable; rules for human errors were not collected.
agent_relevance: Gap 3 partial: test-time compute closed the accuracy gap on a grid abstraction test, but accuracy overstates competence. Do not infer far-analogy competence from a high pass rate; check the stated mapping.

source: Sala, Aksayli, Tatlidil, Tatsumi, Gondo, Gobet (2019) Near and Far Transfer in Cognitive Training: A Second-Order Meta-Analysis. Collabra: Psychology 5(1):18
finding: Full text opened. The search-summary figures (near 0.27, far 0.12) are not the published ones for near; far 0.12 matches. After placebo and publication-bias control, far transfer is about zero.
numbers: Model 1 (near, working-memory training, k=99): naive overall g=0.32, SE 0.03, 95% CI [0.26, 0.38]; PET 0.14, PEESE 0.22; corrected second-order summary row 0.21; active-control-only summary 0.24. Model 2 (far, k=119): overall g=0.12, SE 0.02, 95% CI [0.08, 0.16]; after controlling placebo and bias the overall effect is near null (g=0.01) and true variance zero. Model 3 (k=233, adds video games, music, chess, exergames): g=0.12; per-program far g from 0.04 (video games, older adults) to 0.19 (music, children).
quote: The lack of generalization of skills acquired by training is thus an invariant of human cognition.
limits: About cognitive-training programs for people, not knowledge transfer between problem types. 0.27 and 0.121 seem to come from the preprint. Table extraction is partly garbled, so the 0.21 and 0.24 rows are read with moderate confidence.
agent_relevance: Gap 9 closed with a correction: use near about 0.2 to 0.3, far 0.12 naive and about 0 when bias is controlled. Supports 'near transfer is the safe bet', but it is human training data, so weak support for an agent.

numbers: Zero-generalisation accuracies as extracted: 0.754, 0.488, 0.350, 0.452. Three-generalisation column includes 0.260, 0.160, 0.078, 0.195. Samples: 2,140 per GPT model, 1,876 for humans at zero generalisations.

source: Inani, Kabra, Marupudi, Varma (2025) Modeling Understanding of Story-Based Analogies Using Large Language Models
finding: Story analogy mapping with GPT-4o and Llama-3.1 reaches human level, but the paper notes fragility to paraphrase.
numbers: Conventional prompt accuracy: humans 0.847; GPT-3 0.75; GPT-4o-mini 0.701; GPT-4o 0.823; Llama-3.1-8B 0.653; Llama-3.1-70B 0.854. Cited prior result: GPT-4 86% on original stories fell to 72% on paraphrased; humans 78% to 70%. The self-generated-hint prompt gave GPT-4o 0.741 (other rows' alignment uncertain).
limits: Mapping task (given the pair), not retrieval from a store. 18 problems from Gentner et al. 1993 via Webb et al. 2023. Paraphrase figures are quoted from another study.
agent_relevance: Gap 3 partial: mapping given the pair is near human for 2024 non-reasoning models; retrieving the right analogue (what O7 needs) is harder and still untested for current frontier models.

source: Camposampiero et al. (2025) I-RAVEN-X: Benchmarking Generalization and Robustness of Analogical and Mathematical Reasoning in LLMs and Large Reasoning Models
finding: Reasoning models degrade less than plain LLMs when relations get longer or attribute ranges wider, but still fail under perceptual uncertainty.
numbers: Arithmetic accuracy falls 80.5% to 63.0% for reasoning models vs 59.3% to 4.4% for LLMs; reasoning models lose 61.8% task accuracy under uncertainty.
limits: Symbolic Raven-style matrices, not narrative or cross-domain analogy. Only abstract and introduction read closely.
agent_relevance: Gap 3 partial: test-time compute narrows the gap on systematic generalisation in structured analogy but does not remove it. No ARN-style answer.

source: Kim et al. (2026) Memory Transfer Learning, pool-size and cross-model results (Findings 5 and 6, Table 6)
finding: Gains grow with the number of memories and of source domains (best at 9), and lessons written by one model help others, though self-written lessons do best.
numbers: Table 6 Pass@1 averages, GPT-5-mini as target: zero-shot 0.515; DeepSeek-V3.2 memories 0.518; Qwen3-Coder memories 0.528; GPT-5-mini memories 0.543.
limits: Pool scaling shown on three benchmarks by random subsampling to 1/4, 2/4, 3/4. Gaps of 0.3 to 1 point are likely within noise.
agent_relevance: Gaps 1 and 8: breadth of source classes seems to matter, so a lesson store should cover many classes. Lessons are largely model-agnostic meta-knowledge.

source: Hu et al. (2026) experience reuse study, task-pair design and mechanism (Sections 2.4, 3.2)
finding: Authors explain the harm: raw action scripts from an easier task were locally plausible but ill-suited to the harder task; abstraction drops the script and keeps the guidance. Finer-grained memory can raise forward transfer while causing severe forgetting.
numbers: Design: ALFWorld A 'put X in Y' (95% baseline) and B 'put a clean X in Y' (54% baseline): same wording, different procedure, built to test surface-similar retrieval. BabyAI B baseline 49%.
quote: Negative transfer disproportionately harms the hard cases
limits: Two task pairs; the stated cause is retrieval pollution in a limited context window.
agent_relevance: Gap 6: directly tests surface-similar, procedure-different pairs and finds the cost. Our agent should test the lesson's precondition, not just the wording of the task.
